acceptance: The worktree audit test finishes within a few seconds regardless of worktree count.
The disk-floor test passes and fails based on injected values, not the host's free space.
context: Source: W2 PR B and PR C fast-lane runs on a shared macOS workstation. Related: dlv2-12-hermeticity-leak-detector.
description:
## Problem
Two tests failed in full local `make test-fast` runs during W2 and passed when run alone, which costs reruns and hides real failures:
- tests/integration/worktree/test_worktree_audit.py::test_make_worktree_audit_json_output hit the 120 s pytest-timeout when the machine was loaded; alone the file takes about 76 s, so it has little headroom, and the time grows with the number of worktrees on the machine.
- A UAT disk-floor test failed when free disk space was low (it passed alone after about 1 GB of scratch files was removed). A test that fails because of the host's free space is not hermetic.

## Change
- Make the worktree-audit test independent of the host's worktree count (fixture repository or a bounded fake) so it runs in a few seconds.
- Make the disk-floor test hermetic (inject the free-space value) while keeping a real check where the floor is meant to protect runs.

## Guardrails
- Keep both behaviours covered; never raise a timeout to hide the cost.
